title: Authenticated Web Scanning: Auto-Register, Login, Test Authenticated Surface
goal: For web targets with open registration (like Gruyere /newaccount.gtl), the auth-flow runner should be able to auto-register a test account, obtain a session cookie, and pass that session to subsequent runners (xss-extended, client-state, idor-bac). This requires: (1) auth-flow detecting registration forms from content-discovery links; (2) creating a test account via the registration form; (3) logging in and storing the session token in the run credential vault; (4) subsequent runners receiving that session token via vault injection. Without this, stored XSS, CSRF, path traversal, and client-state manipulation cannot be tested on auth-gated surfaces.
generation_reason: Live Gruyere run found only unauthenticated vulnerabilities (~30% coverage). 70% of Gruyere vulnerabilities require authentication. Open-registration targets like Gruyere can be tested without manual credential setup.
success_criteria: auth-flow detects registration form from content-discovery links and creates a test account.
Session token stored in credential vault and injected into subsequent runners.
xss-extended, client-state, idor-bac run against authenticated endpoints.
Stored XSS in Gruyere snippet submission is found.

constraints.scope_boundary: Only create test accounts on targets that explicitly expose open registration. Never use production credentials.
constraints.vault_only: Session tokens must go through the credential vault, not hardcoded params.
constraints.no_scope_bypass: All authenticated requests must remain within approved scope.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Limit to auth registration and session vault injection.
constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.

acceptance_criteria: auth-flow creates account and obtains session.
Session injected into xss-extended via vault.
Stored XSS found on authenticated snippet endpoint.

out_of_scope: Bypassing approval gates, scope/ROE boundaries, credential protections, or kill-switch behavior.
Running live public target scans without explicit operator authorization.
